story: Mount Unzen is not one mountain but a cluster of volcanic peaks at the heart of the Shimabara Peninsula, built by eruptions over hundreds of thousands of years. Its history is violent. In 1792 an earthquake brought down the flank of Mayuyama, above Shimabara, and the landslide raised a tsunami that crossed the Ariake Sea; about fifteen thousand people died, Japan's worst volcanic disaster. In November 1990 Fugendake erupted after nearly two centuries of quiet, and a lava dome began to grow over its summit.

Over the next five years that dome kept collapsing in pyroclastic flows. On 3 June 1991 one of them swept down the eastern slopes and killed 43 people, three volcanologists among them. When the eruption ended in 1995, the dome had become a new mountain, named Heisei Shinzan in 1996; at 1,483 metres it is the highest point in Nagasaki Prefecture, and still off limits. Below the summit, steam and sulphur pour from the vents of Unzen Jigoku, and in May the slopes of Nita Pass turn pink with Miyama-kirishima azaleas.

The Amakusa Islands, about 120 of them, are made of rock that formed on the sea floor and was later raised above it; on Goshoura it yields dinosaur bones and fossil shellfish. The sea between the islands is calm and rich: Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins live year-round in the strait off the Shimabara Peninsula, and the western cliffs and caves of Shimoshima face the open East China Sea.

This coast was a stronghold of early Christianity in Japan, and in 1637 the Shimabara Rebellion, led by the teenage Amakusa Shirō, broke out among its peasants. Three centuries later Unzen, already a hot-spring resort, became on 16 March 1934 one of Japan's first three national parks, together with Setonaikai and Kirishima. The Amakusa Islands were added on 20 July 1956, and the park took its present name.
howItWorks: Unzen-Amakusa is a regional park in two parts, Unzen on the Shimabara Peninsula in Nagasaki and the Amakusa Islands in Kumamoto, with a corner of Nagashima in Kagoshima. About two-thirds of the land is privately owned and a quarter is national forest. The hot-spring towns of Unzen and Obama, farms, fishing ports and island villages lie within or beside it.

Most of the park is special zone in three classes, where building, felling and digging need permission; only about 2 per cent is special protection zone, and roughly 30 per cent is ordinary zone. Marine park zones off Tomioka, Amakusa and Ushibuka, first designated in 1970, protect the reefs and coral communities of the Amakusa coast.

Mount Unzen is an active volcano watched by the Japan Meteorological Agency, which sets a Volcanic Alert Level from 1 to 5. Heisei Shinzan and the area around the lava dome are closed to entry because of the risk of collapse, and the summit trails close whenever the level rises. The Shimabara Peninsula is also a UNESCO Global Geopark, one of Japan's first three, recognised in 2009, which interprets the eruption and its aftermath.

sightNotes.poi-jp-unzen-amakusa-mount-fugen-and-hei: Climb from Nita Pass to Fugendake's 1,359-metre summit for a close view of the lava dome of 1990–95, the park's newest and highest peak.
sightNotes.poi-jp-unzen-amakusa-nita-pass: Trailheads, a ropeway up towards Myōkendake and views over the volcano. Azaleas in May and colour in autumn.
sightNotes.poi-jp-unzen-amakusa-unzen-jigoku: The 'hells' at Unzen Onsen: boardwalks over steaming, sulphurous vents and bubbling pools in the middle of the hot-spring town.
sightNotes.poi-jp-unzen-amakusa-mount-takabuto-and-: A hilltop lookout over the islets of Amakusa Matsushima, best at sunset.
sightNotes.poi-jp-unzen-amakusa-jusanbutsu-park: A clifftop view over Myōkenura, a scenic place and natural monument on Shimoshima's west coast: sea cliffs, sea caves and an elephant-shaped rock.

chronology.text: The Shimabara Rebellion, led by Amakusa Shirō, breaks out on the peninsula and the islands.
An earthquake collapses Mayuyama; the landslide and tsunami kill about fifteen thousand people.
On 16 March Unzen becomes one of Japan's first three national parks, together with Setonaikai and Kirishima.
The Amakusa Islands are added on 20 July and the park is renamed Unzen-Amakusa.
Marine park zones are designated off Tomioka, Amakusa and Ushibuka, among Japan's first.
Fugendake erupts on 17 November after about two hundred years of quiet.
On 3 June a pyroclastic flow kills 43 people on the volcano's eastern slopes.
The new lava dome is named Heisei Shinzan.
The Shimabara Peninsula becomes one of Japan's first three Global Geoparks.

safety: Mount Unzen is an active volcano. Check the Japan Meteorological Agency's current Volcanic Alert Level before you go; at level 2 the area round the summit craters is closed, at level 3 the mountain.
Never enter the closed zone around Heisei Shinzan; the lava dome is unstable and can still collapse.
Volcanic gas can gather near vents. Keep to the paths at Unzen Jigoku and on the summits, and leave if you feel unwell.
Heavy rain can send debris flows down the valleys below the volcano; heed closures in the rainy season and typhoons.
regulations: Entry to Heisei Shinzan and the restricted zone around it is prohibited.
Stay on boardwalks at Unzen Jigoku; the ground is hot and fragile.
Plants, animals and rocks are protected in the special protection zone and many in the special zones; in the marine park zones, collecting designated marine life needs permission.
On Goshoura, collect fossils at the fossil-collecting site near the port and follow its rules on what may be taken home.

weather: Western Kyushu is warm and wet. Winters are mild on the coast but cold on the volcano. Spring brings the azaleas in May. The rainy season, from June into July, brings heavy rain and the risk of landslides, and typhoons can strike from August to October. Summer is hot and humid on the islands, and the best time for swimming and diving. Autumn brings clear days and colour to the volcano's forests.
directions: From Tokyo, fly to Nagasaki Airport and take a bus to Isahaya, then a Shimatetsu bus up to Unzen Onsen (about an hour and 20 minutes); Nagasaki Kenei Bus also runs express buses from Nagasaki to Unzen. By rail, take the JR line from Nagasaki or the Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen to Isahaya and change to the bus. For Amakusa, fly from Fukuoka or Kumamoto to Amakusa Airport on Shimoshima, or take the JR Misumi Line from Kumamoto to Misumi and a ferry or the road bridges onward. Between the two halves of the park, car ferries cross from Kuchinotsu on the Shimabara Peninsula to Oniike on Shimoshima in about 30 minutes. Buses on Amakusa are sparse; a car is the practical way to see the islands.
